title: Feature/1960
summary: Since the last plan, every round is played in **its own new tab**, so a shared session or another tab is never moved by the game; switching tabs mid-round shows **Return to game**, and closing the round's tab ends the round. Winning now shows a **full-screen celebration** with confetti and a short victory sound on every screen size (with a button to turn the sound off), and the found verse stays marked. **Reveal hint** and **Reveal verse** are now in the bar too, **Reveal verse** keeps the answer lit until the round ends, **every** chance now needs a hint, and **Back to main menu** is renamed **Back to games**. Saved games are stored differently, so games saved on earlier builds no longer appear. Overall the PR adds **Find the Verse**, a new extension with a guessing game: someone creates a game by picking a secret verse and writing hints, then a player taps verses in the reader to guess, and the game says whether the secret verse is earlier or later. Games can be saved to your account to play, edit, or delete later.

links.label: Issue 1960: Port the "find this verse" game for the Bible stack

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the button above, in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer (one section later uses a phone, and one uses a second browser). If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If it looks like the old version, do a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).

setup.title: Turn your sound on
setup.body: Winning now plays a short sound. Turn your computer's volume up a little so you can hear it.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Games are saved to your account, so most tests need you signed in. Open **Settings** (the gear icon), choose to sign in, enter your email address, then type the code that arrives in your inbox. Use an inbox you can check.

setup.title: Install the Find the Verse extension
setup.body: Open the app's menu and go to **Extensions**. If **Find the Verse** isn't already under **Installed**, install it from **Available**. If you can't find **Find the Verse** at all, mark every test **Blocked** and say so in the note.

setup.title: Find the game button
setup.body: A **Find the Verse** button (a crosshair / target icon) appears in the app's toolbar. If you don't see it, look in the toolbar's overflow (**...**) menu. Clicking it opens the game panel at the side of the screen. In these tests, "the panel" means that game panel, "the bar" means the small floating game bar that appears over the reader during a round, and "the tab list" means the list of open reading tabs.

setup.title: Start with no saved games
setup.body: Games saved while testing earlier plans for this PR no longer appear, because this commit stores games differently. That's expected. If you do see any cards under **My saved games**, delete them first (on each card, **...** → **Delete** → **Delete**), so the lists match what the tests describe.

setup.title: Use one English translation
setup.body: Read in an English translation such as **BSB** for every test, so the book names and verse text match what's written here.

sections.title: Creating a game
sections.intro: Make the game the later sections play: secret verse **John 3:16**, four chances.

tests.title: The panel starts with a Create a game button
steps: Click the **Find the Verse** toolbar button.
expected: A panel titled **Find the Verse** opens with a 🔍 icon, a short description of the game, and a **Create a game** button.
No **My saved games** list is shown yet (you haven't saved any).

tests.title: Saving an empty game shows one problem at a time
tests.why: The form checks the name first, then the secret verse, then the hints, and scrolls to whichever is wrong. The hint check is covered in its own test below.
steps: Click **Create a game**.
Without filling anything in, click **Save game** (the second of the two buttons at the bottom; the first is **Start game**).
Type `Test game` in **Game name** and click **Save game** again.
expected: After the first click, a red message **Give this game a name.** appears under the name box.
After the second click, the name message goes away and **Pick the secret verse before saving.** appears under **Secret verse** instead.
No game is saved and the panel stays on the **Create a game** form.

tests.title: Typing a reference picks the secret verse and opens it in the reader
tests.before: Continue on the form from the previous test.
steps: In the box with the placeholder `e.g. John 1:1`, type `John 3:16-17` and click **Go**.
Replace it with `Hezekiah 1:1` and press **Enter**.
Replace it with `John 3:16` and click **Go**.
expected: `John 3:16-17` shows **Pick a single verse, like John 1:1, not a range.**
`Hezekiah 1:1` shows **Couldn't recognise that reference. Try “John 1:1”.**
`John 3:16` shows a grey box reading **John 3:16** with the verse text in italics ("For God so loved the world…"), and the reader jumps to John chapter 3.

tests.title: Select from reader lets you pick the verse by tapping it
tests.why: The second way to choose a secret verse.
tests.before: Continue on the form. John 3:16 is the current secret verse.
steps: Click **Select from reader…**.
In the reader, click verse **John 3:3**.
In the toolbar that appears for the verse, click **Set as target**.
Type `John 3:16` in the reference box and click **Go** again, so the secret verse is back to John 3:16 for the rest of the tests.
expected: After **Select from reader…**, a coloured box says **Tap any verse in the reader, then choose Set as target in the toolbar.** with a **Cancel** button.
The verse toolbar shows a **Set as target** button (with a pin icon) alongside its usual buttons.
After **Set as target**, the coloured box goes away and the preview shows **John 3:3** with its text.
After the last step the preview shows **John 3:16** again.

tests.title: Every chance needs a hint, and you can add or remove chances down to 3
tests.why: Changed since commit `965df14`: there, only 3 hints had to be filled in and the other chances could stay empty. Now every chance needs a hint. Failed on the plan for commit `53bbd66`: "game can be saved with empty chances".
tests.before: Continue on the form (name `Test game`, secret verse John 3:16).
steps: Look at the **Chances** section.
Click the red **×** next to rows 5, 6 and 7 until only four rows are left.
Click **+ Add chance**, then click **×** on the new row.
Fill in hint boxes 1 and 2 only: `New Testament` and `One of the Gospels`. Click **Save game**.
Fill in box 4: type `A very famous verse`, press Enter once, and type `second line`. Click **Save game** again.
Fill in box 3: `Chapter 3`.
expected: At first there are seven empty hint rows, each with the grey placeholder **Hint…**, and the label reads **Chances (7)**. The line under it says **Start with 7. You can add more or remove down to 3. Every chance needs a hint.**
The label counts down as rows are removed, ending at **Chances (4)**; **+ Add chance** makes it 5, and removing that row brings it back to 4.

With two hints filled in, **Save game** shows the red message **Fill in every hint, or remove the empty chances.** under the chances, the empty boxes 3 and 4 are outlined in red, and nothing is saved.
Box 4 grows to show both lines of text. With box 3 still empty, the second **Save game** shows the same red message again and still saves nothing.
As soon as box 3 is filled in, the red message and red outlines go away.

tests.title: Saving the game adds it to My saved games, and it survives a reload
tests.before: The form has name `Test game`, secret verse John 3:16, and four chances, all with hints.
steps: Click **Save game**.
Look at the card under **My saved games**.
Click **Show reference** on the card.
Reload the page, then open the panel again from the toolbar button.
expected: The panel goes back to the start screen, and a **My saved games** list shows one card: **Test game**, a **Show reference** link, and **Saved game · 4 chances · <today's date>**, with a **Play** button and a **...** menu.
The reference is hidden until you click **Show reference**, which replaces the name with **John 3:16**.
After the reload the card is still there.

tests.title: Cancel throws a draft away without saving
steps: Click **Create a game**.
Type `Throwaway` as the name, then click **Cancel**.
Click **Create a game** again.
expected: **Cancel** returns to the start screen and no **Throwaway** card appears.
The new form is blank: empty name, no secret verse, seven empty hints.

tests.title: Start game plays straight from the form in a new tab, without saving
tests.why: Changed since commit `965df14`: the round used to take over the tab you were reading in. Now it opens its own tab, and **End game** closes that tab and takes you back.
tests.before: Continue on the blank form from the previous test. Note which tab is selected in the tab list and which chapter it shows.
steps: Click **Start game** without filling anything in.
Type `Quick round` as the name and click **Start game** again.
Type `Psalm 23:1` in the reference box, click **Go**, and click **Start game** again.
Click **×** on rows until no **×** is left.
Fill in all the remaining hints: `Old Testament`, `Poetry`, `A shepherd`. Click **Start game**.
Look at the tab list.
Click verse **Genesis 1:1** in the reader.
Click **End game** in the bar.
expected: With nothing filled in, **Give this game a name.** appears and no round starts. With only a name, **Pick the secret verse before saving.** appears instead. With a name and verse but empty hints, **Fill in every hint, or remove the empty chances.** appears.
The **×** buttons disappear once there are three rows left (**Chances (3)**).
**Start game** closes the panel and opens a **new tab** on **Genesis 1**, which becomes the selected tab. The tab you were on is still in the tab list, still on Psalm 23.
A bar near the bottom of the reader shows **Quick round**, **3 / 3 left**, a round **?** button, and an **End game** button.
After the guess, the bar shows **2 / 3 left** and **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.**

**End game** removes the bar, closes the game's tab, takes you back to the tab you were on (Psalm 23), and opens the panel on the start screen. Only **Test game** is under **My saved games**; no **Quick round** card was saved.

tests.title: Set as target on any verse starts a new game with that verse
tests.why: Issue 1960 asks for a way to start a game from the verse toolbar.
tests.before: The panel is on the start screen (no round in progress). Close the panel.
steps: Open **Romans 8** and click verse **Romans 8:28**.
In the verse toolbar, click **Set as target**.
Type `From toolbar` as the name.
Without leaving the form, click verse **Romans 8:1** in the reader and click **Set as target** again.
Click **Cancel**.
expected: The verse toolbar shows **Set as target** (pin icon) alongside its usual buttons, even though the game panel is closed.
Clicking it opens the panel on a fresh **Create a game** form with **Romans 8:28** and its text already filled in as the secret verse, an empty name, and seven empty chances.
The second **Set as target** changes the secret verse to **Romans 8:1** and keeps the name `From toolbar`.
**Cancel** returns to the start screen with no new card.

sections.title: Playing a game
sections.intro: Play `Test game` (secret verse John 3:16, four chances). Order matters: tests continue the same round until a test says to start a new one. Starting a round closes the panel; the **Find the Verse** toolbar button reopens it at any time. Stay on the tab showing **Romans 8** before each **Play**, so you can tell when you've been taken back to it.

tests.title: Play opens a new tab at Genesis 1 and starts the round in the bar
tests.why: Changed since commit `965df14`: **Play** used to move the tab you were reading in to Genesis 1. Now the round gets its own tab.
steps: On the **Test game** card, click **Play**.
Look at the tab list.
Click the round **?** button in the bar.
expected: The panel closes, and a new tab opens on **Genesis 1** and is selected. The **Romans 8** tab is still in the tab list.
A bar near the bottom of the reader shows **Test game**, **4 / 4 left**, a **?** button, and an **End game** button. It has rounded corners and a thin border, like the reader's own toolbar.
Clicking **?** replaces it with the first hint: **New Testament**.

tests.title: A wrong book says later or earlier, greys out what's ruled out, and uses a chance
steps: Click verse **Genesis 1:1** in the reader.
Click **Genesis 1:1** again.
Open the book list (the book/chapter picker) and look at **Genesis**.
Click **?** in the bar to see the next hint.
expected: The normal verse toolbar does NOT appear when you click a verse; the click counts as a guess instead.
The bar says **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.** and shows **3 / 4 left**.
Clicking the same verse again shows the same message but does NOT use another chance (still **3 / 4 left**).
The verses of Genesis 1 look faded, and **Genesis** is greyed out in the book list.
The **?** button is back (a new chance means a new hint) and shows **One of the Gospels**.

tests.title: Guessing past the verse says it's earlier, and the reveal buttons appear in the bar at half the chances
tests.why: Changed since commit `965df14`: **Reveal hint** and **Reveal verse** used to be only in the panel, so on a computer you had to know to reopen it. With four chances they appear after two guesses (half, rounded up).
steps: Use the book list to open **Revelation 1**.
Click verse **Revelation 1:1**.
Click **?** in the bar.
Click the **Find the Verse** toolbar button to open the panel. Leave it open for the next tests.
expected: The bar says **The verse is earlier in the Bible — try a book further back.** and shows **2 / 4 left**.
**Revelation** is now greyed out in the book list, as well as Genesis.
**?** shows the third hint: **Chapter 3**.
The bar now also has two buttons, **Reveal hint** and **Reveal verse**.

When the panel opens, the bar disappears. The panel shows the same round: **Test game**, **2 / 4 left**, the last message, **Reveal hint** and **Reveal verse** buttons, **End game**, and a **Victory sound on** button with a speaker icon.

tests.title: Right book and right chapter give their own messages, and the chapter list greys out ruled-out chapters
tests.before: The panel is open, in the middle of the round.
steps: Open **John 1** and click verse **John 1:1**.
Open the chapter list for John and look at chapter 1.
Open **John 3** and click verse **John 3:20**.
expected: After John 1:1: **Right book! The verse is in a later chapter.** and **1 / 4 left**. The **?** button is back and shows the two-line hint **A very famous verse** / **second line**. Chapter 1 is greyed out in John's chapter list.
After John 3:20: **Right chapter! The verse number is lower.** In John 3, verses 20 and after look faded.
The pill now reads **Out of chances** in red, with the message **You've used all your chances, but you can keep guessing — good luck!**

tests.title: Reveal hint blanks out about half the words of the verse
steps: Click **Reveal hint** in the panel.
Close the panel and look at the bar.
expected: A box labelled **PARTIAL HINT** shows the verse with roughly half of its words replaced by `___`, in random places.
The **Reveal hint** button disappears; **Reveal verse** stays.
The bar shows the same partial verse in italics, and only a **Reveal verse** button.

tests.title: Finding the verse shows a full-screen celebration with a sound
tests.why: Changed since commit `965df14`: on a computer, a win used to only change the bar's text to **You found it!**, with no confetti. Now a full-screen celebration with confetti and a short sound shows on every screen size, and the found verse stays marked until the round ends. **Back to main menu** is renamed **Back to games**.
tests.before: The panel is closed and the round is still going in John 3.
steps: Click verse **John 3:16**.
Click **Keep reading**.
Look at John 3:16 in the reader and at the bar.
Click verse **John 3:1** and look at the verse toolbar, if one appears.
Click **Back to games** in the bar.
Click a verse in the reader.
expected: A short rising "ta-da" plays, and confetti falls across the whole screen over the reader. A card in the middle shows 🎉 **You found it!**, **John 3:16**, the verse text in italics, **5 guesses**, a **Back to games** button, a **Keep reading** button, and a **Victory sound on** button.
**Keep reading** closes the celebration. **John 3:16** stays marked with a coloured background, and the bar shows **You found it!** next to a **Back to games** button.
Clicking another verse does not show a **Set as target** button.
**Back to games** removes the bar, closes the game's tab, takes you back to the **Romans 8** tab, and opens the panel on the start screen with the **Test game** card.
Nothing is faded or greyed out, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar, with **Set as target** back in it.

tests.title: The victory sound can be turned off, and stays off
tests.why: New since commit `965df14`. The choice is remembered on this device.
steps: Click **Play** on **Test game**, then open the panel with the toolbar button.
Click **Victory sound on**.
Close the panel. Open **John 3** and click verse **John 3:16**.
Press the **Esc** key.
Click **Back to games** in the bar. Reload the page.
Click **Play** on **Test game**, open the panel, and look at the sound button.
Click it to turn the sound back on, then click **End game** in the panel.
expected: The button changes to **Victory sound off** with a crossed-out speaker icon.
The win shows the celebration and confetti but makes **no sound**. Its sound button reads **Victory sound off**.
**Esc** closes the celebration, the same as **Keep reading**.
After the reload, the panel's button still reads **Victory sound off**.
Clicking it switches back to **Victory sound on**. **End game** returns the panel to the start screen, closes the game's tab, and takes you back to Romans 8.

tests.title: Reveal verse in the bar shows the answer and keeps it lit
tests.why: Changed since commit `965df14`: the lit verse and dimmed chapter used to go back to normal after about 3 seconds. Now they stay until the round ends.
steps: Click **Play** on **Test game**.
Click **Genesis 1:1**, then open **Revelation 1** and click **Revelation 1:1**.
Click **Reveal verse** in the bar.
Wait 10 seconds.
Click another verse in the reader.
Open the panel with the toolbar button.
expected: **Play** opens a fresh game tab at **4 / 4 left**, with nothing greyed out from the last round.
**Reveal verse** opens **John 3**, scrolls to verse 16, and lights it up while the rest of the chapter is dimmed.
After 10 seconds verse 16 is still lit and the rest still dimmed.
The bar says **Better luck next time — keep going!** and the reveal buttons are gone.
Clicking another verse does not count as a guess and does not open the normal verse toolbar.
The panel shows **John 3:16** with the full verse text and **Better luck next time — keep going!**

tests.title: End game in the panel stops the round
tests.before: Continue from the revealed round in the previous test, with the panel open.
steps: Click **End game** in the panel.
Click a verse in the reader.
expected: The panel returns to the start screen. The game's tab closes and you're back on the **Romans 8** tab.
Nothing is dimmed, and clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar.

sections.title: Rounds stay in their own tab
sections.intro: New since commit `965df14`. A round used to follow whichever tab was selected, which in a shared session moved everyone in it.

tests.title: Switching to another tab mid-round leaves that tab alone
steps: Click **Play** on **Test game**, and click verse **Genesis 1:1**.
In the tab list, click the **Romans 8** tab.
Look at the bar, then click verse **Romans 8:28**.
Open the book list and look at **Genesis**.
Click **Return to game** in the bar.
expected: On the Romans 8 tab the bar says **Your game is in another tab.** with a **Return to game** button. It still shows **3 / 4 left**.
Clicking Romans 8:28 opens the normal verse toolbar (without **Set as target**) and does not use a chance: the bar still shows **3 / 4 left**.
Nothing is faded in Romans 8, and **Genesis** is NOT greyed out in the book list while you're on this tab.
**Return to game** switches back to the game's tab on Genesis 1, which is still faded. The bar shows the last message again.

tests.title: Closing the game's tab ends the round
tests.before: Continue the round from the previous test, on the game's tab.
steps: In the tab list, close the game's tab (the one showing Genesis 1).
Click a verse in the reader.
Open the panel with the toolbar button.
expected: The bar disappears and the reader shows another tab.
Clicking a verse opens the normal verse toolbar, with **Set as target** in it.
The panel shows the start screen, not a round in progress.

tests.title: Playing in a shared session doesn't move anyone else
tests.why: Before this commit, **Play** in a shared session sent everyone in it to Genesis 1, made them follow every guess, and **Reveal verse** showed them the answer.

setup.title: Start a shared session with a second browser
setup.body: You need a second browser or a private/incognito window (it can stay signed out). In your main browser, open **John 3**, click **Share** (the share icon at the top of the tabs side bar), then **Start and share session**. A link is copied to your clipboard. Paste it into the second window and open it, doing a hard refresh there once if the page looks old. Keep both windows side by side if you can.

tests.before: Your main browser has the session tab selected, on John 3.
steps: In your main browser, open the panel and click **Play** on **Test game**.
Click verse **Genesis 1:1**, open **Revelation 1** and click **Revelation 1:1**, then click **Reveal verse** in the bar.
Watch the second window throughout.
Click **End game** in the bar.
expected: **Play** opens a new tab on Genesis 1 in your main browser; the session tab stays on John 3 in your tab list.
The second window stays on **John 3** the whole time. It never jumps to Genesis or Revelation, nothing in it is faded or greyed out, and verse 16 is not lit up after **Reveal verse**.
**End game** closes the game's tab and takes your main browser back to the session tab on John 3.

tests.title: Picking a secret verse in a session tab doesn't show it to anyone else
tests.before: Still in the shared session from the previous test, with the session tab selected on John 3 and the second window open.
steps: In your main browser, click **Create a game**.
Type `Psalm 23:1` in the reference box and click **Go**.
Watch both windows, then click **Cancel**.
Afterwards, end the session and close the second window.
expected: The preview in the panel shows **Psalm 23:1** with its text.
Your main browser's reader stays on **John 3** (outside a session, **Go** would jump there), and the second window stays on **John 3** too.

tests.title: Edit changes the saved game instead of adding a copy
steps: On the **Test game** card, open the **...** menu and choose **Edit**.
Change the name to `Test game edited`, click **×** on row 3 (**Chapter 3**), and click **Save game**.
Reload the page and open the panel.
expected: The form title reads **Edit game**, with the name, the John 3:16 preview, and the four hints you wrote (4 still showing both lines). The first button at the bottom reads **Save & Start** instead of **Start game**.
After removing row 3 there are three rows and no **×** buttons.
After saving there is still only one card: **Test game edited**, **3 chances**, with the original date.
It is still there after the reload.

tests.title: Save & Start saves your edits, then starts the round
steps: On **Test game edited**, open **...** and choose **Edit**.
Clear hint 2 (delete all its text) and click **Save & Start**.
Type `In the Gospels` in hint 2 and click **Save & Start** again.
Click verse **Genesis 1:1**, then click **?** in the bar.
Click **End game** in the bar. Open **...** → **Edit** on the card again, look at hint 2, then click **Cancel**.
expected: With hint 2 empty, **Fill in every hint, or remove the empty chances.** appears and no round starts.
With all three hints filled in, the panel closes and the round starts in a new tab at **Genesis 1** with **3 / 3 left** in the bar.
After the guess, **?** shows **In the Gospels**.
When you edit the game again, hint 2 still reads **In the Gospels**: the change was saved. There is still only one card.

tests.title: Delete asks first, and Cancel keeps the game
steps: On the card, open **...** and choose **Delete**.
Click **Cancel**.
Open **...** again, choose **Delete**, then click **Delete**.
Reload the page and open the panel.
expected: The card shows **Delete this game?** with **Delete** and **Cancel** buttons in place of **Play**.
**Cancel** puts the card back as it was.
**Delete** removes the card, and the **My saved games** heading disappears with it.
After the reload the game is still gone.

tests.title: Saved games stay on your account and follow you to another browser
steps: Create and save a new game: name `Second browser`, secret verse `Psalm 23:1`, and three chances (remove rows down to three), each with a hint of your choice.
In a different browser (or a private/incognito window), open the preview, sign in with the same email, install **Find the Verse** if needed, and open the panel.
expected: The **Second browser** card appears there too, with **3 chances**.

tests.title: Saving in one browser doesn't erase a game saved in another
tests.why: Saving used to write back only this browser's copy of your list, silently deleting a game saved elsewhere in the meantime.
tests.before: Keep both browsers from the previous test open and signed in to the same account, with the panel open in both. Don't reload either one.
steps: In the first browser, create and save a game named `One` (any verse, three hints).
In the second browser, without reloading, create and save a game named `Two` (any verse, three hints).
Close and reopen the panel in each browser (don't reload).
expected: Both browsers list **One**, **Two** and **Second browser**. No game is missing.
Reopening the panel doesn't blank the list: the cards stay on screen while it refreshes.

tests.title: Deleting a game that was already deleted in another browser removes its card
tests.before: Both browsers from the previous test, panel open in both, showing **One**.
steps: In the first browser, delete **One** (**...** → **Delete** → **Delete**).
In the second browser, without reloading or reopening the panel, delete **One** the same way.
expected: In both browsers the **One** card disappears, with no error. **Two** and **Second browser** are still listed.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The normal verse toolbar still works, with one extra button
tests.why: **Set as target** shows on every verse for anyone with the extension installed (except during a round), so check it doesn't get in the way.
steps: Click any verse, and use the toolbar to highlight it in a colour.
Click the verse again and remove the highlight.
Go to **Extensions**, uninstall **Find the Verse**, then click a verse.
expected: Highlighting and removing a highlight work as before. **Set as target** sits among the usual buttons without pushing any off the toolbar.
After uninstalling, **Set as target** is gone from the toolbar. Reinstall the extension if you have more tests to do.

sections.title: Signed out, phone, and dark mode

tests.title: Signed out, you can play a game but not save it
tests.before: Open the preview in a private/incognito window and don't sign in. Install **Find the Verse** from **Extensions** if it lets you; if it requires signing in, mark this test **Skip**.
steps: Open the panel and click **Create a game**.
Fill in the name `Guest game` and secret verse `John 1:1`. Click **×** until no **×** is left, and fill in the three hints (any text).
Click **Sign in to save games**.
Click **Start game**, then click verse **Genesis 1:1**.
expected: No **My saved games** list is shown.
The buttons read **Start game** and **Sign in to save games**. Clicking **Sign in to save games** shows the red message **Sign in to save games** and nothing is saved.
**Start game** closes the panel, opens a new tab on **Genesis 1**, and shows the bar with **3 / 3 left**; the guess says **The verse is later in the Bible — try a book further along.**

tests.title: On a phone, picking a secret verse works with the panel closed
tests.before: On a phone, signed in, with the extension installed.
steps: Open the panel, tap **Create a game**, then **Select from reader…**.
Close the panel.
Tap any verse, then tap **Set as target** in the verse toolbar.
Tap **Cancel** to throw the draft away.
expected: With the panel closed, a bar over the reader says **Tap any verse in the reader, then choose Set as target in the toolbar.** with a **Cancel** button. The whole bar is visible, not hidden behind the app's bottom bars.
After **Set as target** the panel reopens by itself and shows the verse you picked.

tests.title: On a phone, the game bar stays visible and the win fills the screen
tests.why: Changed since commit `965df14`: a win on a phone used to reopen the panel to show a small strip of confetti. Now the same full-screen celebration as on a computer shows over the reader, and the reveal buttons are in the bar.
tests.before: On a phone, signed in, with the **Second browser** game saved (secret verse Psalm 23:1, three chances). Turn the phone's sound on.
steps: Tap **Play** on **Second browser**.
Tap two verses outside Psalms to guess, then scroll the chapter down and back up.
Tap **More** in the bottom tab bar, then close that menu.
Open **Psalm 23** and tap verse **Psalm 23:1**.
Tap **Back to games**.
expected: **Play** closes the panel by itself and opens a new tab on Genesis 1. The bar sits just above the app's bottom bars. Its name, chances, **?**, latest message and **End game** are all fully visible and nothing runs off the side of the screen.
After two guesses the bar also shows **Reveal hint** and **Reveal verse**, still fully visible.
When scrolling makes the bottom bars slide down, the game bar moves down with them and stays fully visible; it comes back up when they do.
While the **More** menu is open the game bar is hidden, so it doesn't cover the menu. Closing the menu brings the bar back with the round still going.

Finding the verse plays the short sound and shows the full-screen celebration with confetti, **You found it!**, **Psalm 23:1**, the verse text, and the buttons, all fitting on the screen. The panel does NOT open by itself.
**Back to games** closes the celebration and the game's tab and opens the panel on the start screen.

tests.title: Everything is readable in dark mode
steps: Switch the app to dark mode in **Settings**.
Look at the start screen, the **Create a game** form (including a red error message), a round in play (panel and bar, with the reveal buttons showing), and the full-screen win celebration.
expected: All text, boxes, buttons and the greyed-out books and chapters are readable against the dark background. The bar and its buttons match the dark reader toolbar. The celebration card is dark too. Nothing shows as dark text on a dark box or a bright white box.

notCovered: Behaviour when loading, saving or deleting games fails on the server (the "Couldn't save that game" style messages). These are hard to trigger by hand and are covered by automated tests.
Reopening the panel in the split second while a save is still being written. It's too quick to do by hand and is covered by automated tests.
Games saved on earlier builds of this PR. They're stored the old way and are no longer read; none exist outside testing, since the extension hasn't been released.
Turning on "reduce motion" in your device's accessibility settings should stop the confetti from falling. This is optional to check.
Other languages: the game's text is only written in English so far.

Issue 1960 describes Phase 1 as local only (no saving or sharing). This PR saves games to your account and stores each game on its own so sharing can be added later; sharing itself isn't part of this PR.
